t: Siam’s kingdom under the Chakri dynasty, ruled from Bangkok, which Rama I founded in 1782 after deposing Taksin.
It dominated the Lao states, western Cambodia and the northern Malay sultanates before European pressure forced cessions.
Mongkut and Chulalongkorn modernised the state and kept Siam independent until the 1932 revolution ended absolute rule.
dyk: Mongkut spent 27 years as a Buddhist monk before becoming king in 1851, founding the reformist Thammayut order and studying Western astronomy.
ev: Rama I founds the Chakri dynasty and moves the capital to Bangkok
Siam defeats Burma’s invasion in the Nine Armies War
Siamese forces crush Anouvong’s rebellion and sack Vientiane
The Bowring Treaty with Britain opens Siam to Western trade
French gunboats force the Chao Phraya; Siam cedes the lands east of the Mekong
The Slave Abolition Act completes the end of slavery
Siam joins the First World War on the Allied side
The People’s Party’s bloodless revolution ends absolute monarchy
